summary: Completed WU14-02 with a reusable bounded benchmark core, current-process sampler adapter, typed Tauri diagnostics API, and minimal Settings diagnostics UI.
completed: Resolved the packaging decision as local workspace crate pihub-benchmark-core, with no Pi-Hub, SSH, Docker, or Tauri imports.
Implemented one-active-session lifecycle, bounded samples/duration, aggregate operation measurements, explicit in-memory report retrieval/export, RuntimeSampler, and deterministic fake sampler.
Added typed start, stop, status, and report Tauri commands plus a Settings Performance Diagnostics panel without idle polling.
Implemented reliable Windows current-process working set, private bytes, and handle count sampling; deliberately excluded unreliable WebView2 child-process attribution.

validationCommands.summary: Three core tests pass: inactive no-op, single bounded session, and aggregate-only operation records.
Typed frontend diagnostics command boundary test passes.
Rust check/tests/build, frontend tests/build/lint, AIQT status, and diff check passed; lint retained four pre-existing warnings.

acceptanceCriteria.evidence: Core rejects a concurrent start, caps samples and duration, and stops idempotently into an in-memory report.
The Tauri adapter only spawns a sampler after start; its loop exits on inactive state. Core inactive measurement returns before state locking or allocation.

acceptanceCriteria.criterion: Core has no Pi-Hub domain/SSH/Docker/Tauri imports
acceptanceCriteria.evidence: The isolated workspace crate depends only on serde and uuid; platform/Tauri adapters remain in Pi-Hub.
The report contains normalized labels and aggregates only; the Settings UI exports explicit JSON, and no identity/credential/raw-command fields are accepted by the core.

notes: Risk score: 32/100 (medium): a new bounded Tauri state/API and local workspace crate are added, with no existing monitoring instrumentation or runtime policy change.

Windows samples only the Pi-Hub process using direct APIs. WebView2 child-process attribution is intentionally unavailable because a reliable ownership relation is not available without fragile heuristics.
